meta.title: Dux
meta.description: My features and bug fixes in Dux Shell, a desktop shell for Wayland compositors, with the live state of their pull requests, and the music player and Cast plugin I build for it.
meta.lede: I'm a contributor to Dux Shell, a desktop shell for Wayland compositors. This page shows the features I built, the bugs I fixed, and the music player and Cast plugin I build for it.

summary: Dux Player is a music player for Linux in the style of Dux Shell. It runs natively in the shell, with its settings and theme, or standalone in any other shell, and plays local libraries and streams from Navidrome, Subsonic and Jellyfin servers. A Go daemon handles playback, the library and the servers. The window is QML on Quickshell.

Rules keep server tracks on the device (favorites, most played, an album or a playlist), and the server catalogs are stored locally. Browsing and search keep working while a server is unreachable. When the queue ends, the player can continue with similar tracks, picked from the artists, genres and playlists of the whole session. Lyrics are fetched automatically from the server or from online sources, matched to the track and synced word by word, and their timing can be matched to the audio.

It scrobbles to ListenBrainz and Last.fm, casts through dux-cast, the helper behind the Cast plugin, and has custom pages with their own filter rules and columns and a CLI for keybinds and status bars. The bar, the side panel and the full view come in a Bento and a Material style, with elements the user can arrange. I check the interface with headless scenarios against a fake Subsonic server, including the animations frame by frame. The player is still an alpha.

Dux Plugins holds my plugins for Dux Shell. The first one, Cast, mirrors the screen with sound to Chromecast, Google TV and AirPlay devices and plays files, music, playlists, slideshows and links on Chromecast, from the bar or the Control Center. Files a device can't play, such as 8K video or HEIC photos, are converted on the GPU first. Its device handling lives in dux-cast, which Dux Player casts through as well.
dux-cast is the helper program behind Cast, written in Go. One helper runs per user, and every app connected to it sees and controls the same cast. Dux Player casts through it as well.
